boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Dranesville record (December 20, 1861) in McClellan's Operations in Northern Virginia [October-December 1861]. The Confederate forage expedition and McCall's supporting movements are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero; NPS calls Stuart's force brigade-sized. Ord took his brigade, the First Rifles, Easton's battery and two cavalry squadrons, and says prisoners reported four regiments and a six-gun battery under Stuart. Stuart reported four regiments and four guns, 'say 1,200 strong', on December 21, and on December 23 an aggregate of 1,600 infantry with 150 cavalry and four guns; he put the enemy at five to ten regiments with six or seven guns ('They said 3,100') and, from citizens, fifteen regiments.
claims.rationale: Stuart's two figures differ, as do the gun counts. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Ord says the attack came from a thickly wooded hill on his right, with the Confederate guns about 500 yards off in a road he could enfilade. Stuart says his infantry was screened in dense pines, but his guns had no outlet from the road for a mile and the enemy's battery raked the straight road behind them.
claims.rationale: Ground from the two commanders' reports; the sketches are not in OCR.

claims.value: NPS says Stuart was protecting a foraging expedition, and Stuart says his task was to cover all the wagons the army could spare, all of which reached camp safely. Ord says his brigade marched 24 miles, loaded its wagons with forage and carried its wounded back while the division's ambulances lay empty at Washington.
claims.rationale: Supply statements from the two commanders and a summary; no quartermaster return inspected.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Brigadier General J.E.B. Stuart and Brigadier General Edward O.C. Ord; the live page gives Ord as Brigadier General and 'James Stuart' without rank. Ord says he placed the guns himself and pushed the infantry forward, and that McCall arrived between 3 and 4 p.m. and directed him to continue; Reynolds's brigade arrived too late. Stuart says he directed the regiments' positions, withdrew the battery and then ordered the regiments to disengage.
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two reports; McCall's own reports were not selected. No automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory; NPS says Stuart withdrew in mid-afternoon after ensuring his wagons were safe. Ord says the enemy fled, leaving arms, horses, caissons and some dead and wounded; Stuart says he withdrew in perfect order after about two hours as enemy reinforcements arrived, and calls it a success because the wagons were saved.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields read 301 (US 71; CS 230). Ord reports 7 killed and 60 wounded (read 'GO' in OCR), estimates the Confederate dead left on the field at 50 to 75 and says 21 badly wounded were left behind. Stuart's table totals 43 killed, 143 wounded and 8 missing, noting that only 27 were found dead on the field, and says the enemy lost over 50 killed.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: McCall's reports and order (read in part, not selected), the Union regimental reports (Nos. 3-9) and casualty return (No. 10), and the Confederate regimental reports remain deferred; Stuart's sketch and Ord's sketch are not in OCR.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Ord's December 21, 1861 report (Official Records Series I, Volume V) is one family of interested Union accounts. Stuart's December 21 telegram and December 23, 1861 report (same volume) are one family of interested Confederate accounts; the same author has the registered groups stuart-bristoe-reports and stuart-gettysburg-reports. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. No Scribner Campaigns of the Civil War volume narrating this engagement was inspected; Nicolay's volume ends in July 1861.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
